summary: Impersonation of `viem` under unrelated scope with aliased same-scope `abitype` dependency
details: Package `@wrenfield/viem` reproduces the `viem` library (homepage https://viem.sh, repository github.com/wevm/viem) under an unrelated `@wrenfield` scope. The package.json aliases its `abitype` dependency to `npm:@wrenfield/abitype@1.2.3`, a sibling package under the same impersonator scope, so installing `@wrenfield/viem` silently pulls `@wrenfield/abitype` instead of the genuine `abitype` from the @wevm maintainers. The viem source files in this tarball appear to be a clean copy of upstream, but the dependency-aliasing redirects a core transitive into the same impersonator-controlled scope, and any installer reaching for `viem` who lands on this scope will get attacker-controlled code paths through that alias regardless of viem's content here. Routing to human review to confirm scope ownership, assess `@wrenfield/abitype@1.2.3` content, and decide on a public advisory and registry takedown.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
